citeAs: Yuxuan Bian, Xin Chen, Zenan Li, Tiancheng Zhi, Shen Sang, Linjie Luo, Qiang Xu (2025). Video-As-Prompt: Unified Semantic Control for Video Generation. arXiv:2510.20888.
creator: Yuxuan Bian, Xin Chen, Zenan Li, Tiancheng Zhi, Shen Sang, Linjie Luo, Qiang Xu (ByteDance, The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
description: VAP-Data is the largest dataset for semantic-controlled video generation, containing over 100K curated paired videos across 100 semantic conditions. It covers 4 primary categories: concept (entity transformation and interaction), style, motion (human and non-human), and camera movement. The dataset was bootstrapped by curating ~2K high-quality real images and using commercial visual-effects model APIs and community LoRAs to generate paired reference and target videos.
name: VAP-Data
rai:annotationsPerItem: For the user study evaluation benchmark (48 test samples), each video pair was evaluated by 20 video-generation researchers in pairwise comparisons across all methods.
rai:annotatorDemographics: User study participants: 20 randomly selected video-generation researchers who evaluated video quality and semantic alignment via pairwise preference comparisons.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Commercial model APIs: VIDU (vidu.com) and Kling (klingai.kuaishou.com) for video generation; Civitai community LoRAs for additional semantic conditions. User study conducted with 20 video-generation researchers (platform not specified).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Paired videos were generated automatically using commercial visual-effects templates (VIDU and Kling APIs) and community LoRAs applied to curated reference images. Each reference image was matched to all compatible semantic condition templates to produce paired (reference video, target video) samples. For evaluation, 24 semantic conditions were evenly sampled from 4 categories with 2 samples each (48 test samples total). A user study with 20 video-generation researchers evaluated semantic alignment and overall quality via pairwise preference comparisons.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is synthetic and derived from other generative models (commercial APIs and community LoRAs), which may cause VAP to inherit the specific stylistic biases, artifacts, and conceptual limitations of the source templates. For example, if the source models are poor at generating hands, VAP will likely not learn to generate hands well from this data. The semantic conditions in VAP-Data are relatively limited and synthetic. The paper acknowledges that building a large, real-world, semantic-controlled video dataset would help address these issues but is left for future work.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was bootstrapped by curating approximately 2K high-quality real images from the Internet, spanning men, women, children, animals, objects, landscapes, and multi-subject cases. These images were then matched to visual-effects templates from commercial models (VIDU and Kling) and community LoRAs to create paired reference and target videos. Each image was matched to all compatible templates (some templates restrict subject categories), yielding over 100K paired video samples across 100 semantic conditions.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Approximately 2K high-quality real images collected from the Internet, covering diverse subjects: men, women, children, animals, objects, landscapes, and multi-subject cases. These images served as the source material for generating paired video datasets using commercial model APIs and community LoRAs.
rai:dataLimitations: VAP-Data has several limitations: (1) The dataset is synthetic and derived from other generative models (commercial APIs and LoRAs), potentially inheriting stylistic biases, artifacts, and conceptual limitations of source templates. (2) The semantic conditions are relatively limited compared to the full diversity of real-world semantic controls. (3) The dataset was created using visual effects templates from commercial models (VIDU, Kling) and community LoRAs, so it may not generalize to all real-world scenarios. (4) Building a large, real-world, semantic-controlled video dataset is acknowledged as needed but left for future work.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For training, videos were resized to 480p (480×720 or 832) resolution and sampled at 49 frames at 16fps. The dataset was scaled from 1K to 100K training pairs to study scalability. For evaluation, 24 semantic conditions were evenly sampled from 4 categories with 2 samples each (48 test samples total).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Reference images were curated for quality and diversity. Each image was matched to all compatible visual-effects templates (some templates restrict subject categories, e.g., human-only or animal-only). Videos were resized to 480×720 (832) resolution and sampled at 49 frames at 16fps for training.
rai:dataSocialImpact: VAP and VAP-Data target semantic-controlled video generation for research, education, and creative prototyping. The paper notes potential misuse risks including identity impersonation, deepfake content, targeted harassment, deceptive political messaging, and generation of sexualized or violent media. Mitigations include a research-only release, an acceptable-use policy (AUP) prohibiting abusive or unlawful scenarios, and default content filters blocking clearly harmful categories (e.g., sexual content, explicit violence, hate symbols). The dataset is not intended for surveillance, impersonation, political persuasion, or other high-risk deployments.
rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluating unified semantic-controlled video generation models. Specifically intended for research into concept-guided generation (entity transformation, interaction), style-guided generation, motion-guided generation, and camera-guided generation. Also intended to catalyze future research in generalizable semantic video control.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Commercial video generation APIs (VIDU and Kling image-to-video special effects) and community LoRAs (from Civitai) were used to generate paired videos from reference images. Gemini-2.5-Pro was used for automatic semantic alignment scoring in evaluation. GPT-5 was also used for validation of the semantic alignment metric.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes images and videos of people (men, women, children) collected from the Internet, as well as generated videos depicting human subjects. The paper acknowledges misuse risks including identity impersonation and deepfake content, and states the dataset will be released with a research-only license and acceptable-use policy.

null_reasons.license: The paper states a research-only license with an AUP will accompany any artifact release, but no specific named license (e.g., CC-BY, MIT) is stated for VAP-Data itself.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific timeframe or date range for data collection is mentioned in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper does not discuss missing data handling; some templates restrict subject categories but this is described as a design constraint, not missing data.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol is described for VAP-Data; the dataset consists of generated video pairs without missing value imputation.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No inter-annotator agreement metrics or formal annotation quality analysis are reported for the dataset construction process (which was automated). The user study reports preference rates but not annotation agreement statistics.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning, update cadence, or maintenance plan is described for VAP-Data beyond the initial release.
